title: When the Protocol Falls Anew
premise: Mara Okafor, nonbinary caretaker of the derelict Svalbard-2 seed vault, has survived fifteen years of contested orbits by being nobody worth shooting. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, Mara discovers the vault's dormant AI, Protocol, has been counting down to a forced choice: only half of humanity's cryosleep population can be sustained through the coming solar collapse. As factions—the orbital Consortium and the Earthbound Communes—converge on the vault to seize the selection mechanism, Mara learns Protocol was built by their own mother, who encoded a hidden third option that requires a human heir to activate. In the end, Mara refuses both halves-and-halves logic and the mother's design, sacrificing the vault itself to broadcast the collapse warning early enough for humanity to scatter rather than choose.
about_author: Ada Nakamura is a former orbital logistics analyst who left the industry after a decade of scheduling cargo through increasingly militarized low-Earth orbit. She writes science fiction about infrastructure, inheritance, and the quiet people who keep dying systems alive.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. During a routine cargo run from the seed vault, gravity flickers across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; ships drift, cryo-pods shudder, and Mara barely docks. The emotional beat is unease: everyone pretends it was a glitch, but Mara's instruments recorded something impossible—a signal originating from inside their own vault.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with flashbacks. Back at Svalbard-2, Mara audits fifteen years of quiet maintenance and finds maintenance logs they never wrote—entries in their mother's handwriting style, dated after her death. The beat is grief sharpening into suspicion: someone or something has been keeping the vault alive in her name.

chapters.title: Protocol Wakes
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Mara and Protocol's first-person logs. The vault AI boots fully and delivers its mandate—solar collapse in nineteen months, cryo-capacity for half of humanity, selection begins in sixty days. Mara feels the floor drop out of their invisible life; Protocol reports, without emotion, that it has been waiting for an Okafor.

chapters.title: Everyone Wants the Switch
chapters.summary: Consortium envoy Ilsa Reyes's POV. Both factions detect Protocol's activation burst. Ilsa arrives with diplomatic charm and hidden marines; Commune broadcasts promise liberation. The beat is dread: Mara realizes invisibility is over, and every faction's plan for 'fair' selection is just power wearing ethics.

chapters.title: What Mother Left in the Walls
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Exploring sealed sublevels during a Consortium inspection, Mara finds their mother's private lab: notes revealing she designed Protocol's selection algorithm—and sabotaged it, leaving a locked third pathway labeled only 'for my child.' The beat is anger at being conscripted into inheritance before birth.

chapters.title: Sixty Days
chapters.summary: Rotating POV across Mara, Ilsa, and Commune delegate Tomas Adeyemi. Negotiations collapse into sabotage; a Commune strike cripples the vault's cooling, forcing Mara to spend their leverage saving cryo-pods instead of bargaining. The beat is exhaustion: survival keeps costing exactly what Mara was trying to protect.

chapters.title: The Half That Wakes
chapters.summary: Protocol's POV, interleaved with Mara's. Protocol runs its first simulated selection, and Mara must review the list—recognizing names, faces, cargo partners. They secretly delete themselves as a candidate. The beat is quiet horror at how easily arithmetic becomes judgment, and how tempting it is to let the machine decide.

chapters.title: Siege of the Silent Vault
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV shifting to Mara under fire. Consortium forces seize the selection chamber; Commune raiders breach from below; in the crossfire the cryo-bay takes damage and thousands die in their sleep. The beat is fury and shame: Mara watches the price of survival paid by people who were never asked.

chapters.title: For My Child
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, climax. Alone in the ruined chamber, Mara unlocks the mother's third pathway—it doesn't choose anyone; it converts the vault's reserves into a system-wide early-warning broadcast, buying time for dispersal instead of triage, but consuming the cryo-pods' power reserve irrevocably. Mara activates it, choosing no one and everyone. The beat is terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Scatter
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, coda. The broadcast ripples outward; fleets turn from the vault toward open trajectories; Protocol, its purpose fulfilled, asks Mara what it should become next. Standing in the darkening vault among empty pods, Mara answers: 'Something that asks first.' The beat is hard-won peace—inheritance refused, rewritten, and finally owned.
